items.title: Show HN: Knowl – CLAUDE.md hit 1000 lines, so I built memory that prunes itself
items.why_it_matters: An indie developer built Knowl to solve the problem of LLM agents getting confused by bloated, stale context files. It breaks project knowledge into small 'atoms' and automatically prunes old information. This is highly relevant to you because keeping your CLAUDE.md file clean is essential for keeping Claude Code on track as your AI-ingest repo grows. Try this week: Clone the repo and use its pruning logic to clean up your current CLAUDE.md file so Claude stops hallucinating old Next.js configurations.

items.title: Claude Code status line for worktree, branch, context and quota
items.why_it_matters: A developer shipped a terminal status line tool specifically for Claude Code that displays your current git worktree, branch, context, and remaining token quota. Since you are currently learning proper Git discipline on your AI-ingest repo, having your branch and Claude quota visible in real-time prevents accidental commits and unexpected API bills. Try this week: Install the tool and add it to your terminal profile so you can monitor your active Supabase branch while vibe coding.

items.title: Show HN: Faber, cost-efficient open-source coding agent that uses code graph
items.why_it_matters: Faber is a new, open-source coding agent designed to be highly cost-efficient by using a code graph to navigate your codebase instead of sending entire files to the LLM. Since you previously rated cost-saving agent setups highly, this is a direct way to reduce your development expenses. Try this week: Run npm install -g faberwright and run it on a test branch of your AI-ingest project to see if it resolves Next.js import errors cheaper than Claude Code.

items.title: Claude Code Adds Concise Output Style Option
items.why_it_matters: Claude Code has added a new concise output style option to reduce terminal clutter and save on output token costs. This matters to you because shorter terminal outputs directly translate to faster response times and lower API bills during long vibe-coding sessions. Try this week: Run your next Claude Code session with the concise flag enabled to see if it speeds up your Next.js debugging loop.

items.title: Show HN: SkillWorks – every Claude Code skill, scored on whether it loads
items.why_it_matters: SkillWorks is a new directory that aggregates Claude Code skills (MCP tools) and scores them based on whether they successfully load. This makes it easy to extend your terminal agent's capabilities without writing custom integration code from scratch. Try this week: Browse the directory to find a verified Git or Supabase skill and load it into your Claude Code config to automate your database migrations.

items.title: Show HN: Structo – Claude Code for short form writing
items.why_it_matters: Structo is a new terminal-based writing tool designed to bring the fast, keyboard-driven experience of Claude Code to short-form writing. Since you are currently building a news brief tool, this interface can help you quickly draft and edit the layout of your daily summaries. Try this week: Run Structo in your terminal to draft the onboarding copy or README for your AI-ingest project.
